solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: read the wrong way means the synonym for dug is spelt backwards

parts.note: dug as in excavated, as a mine is worked: mined

explanation.surface: A complaint that some fabric was excavated or folded in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns MINED round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill cloth, the stuff of jeans, so it is a kind of material.

definitions.meaning: the soft fine plumage of birds, as stuffed into pillows
someone knocked ... is lying on the floor, as a boxer is ...

explanation.surface: A question about plumage lying on the ground, as after a pillow fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is both soft plumage and the state of having fallen, so one word fits both senses.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows, spanning the words

explanation.surface: A number that applies during an animal's winter sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' signals the hiding place: hibernatioN IN Effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a whole number, the one after eight.

indicators.note: cream that is whipped is beaten about, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Whipped cream offered instead of a scoundrel, as if in a cookery mix-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, close to a rascal or rogue.

clue.text: Chasing record, leftist gradually came to the point

indicators.note: one thing chasing another follows behind it, so the leftist goes after the record

parts.note: a tape is a recording, a record of sound
a red is a communist or left-winger

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist pursuing a record before getting to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that tapers narrows bit by bit until it ends in a point.

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or said, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a throne is a monarch's seat, the symbol of royal power

explanation.surface: A news item about a ruler's chair being thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals that THRONE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thrown away or out has been got rid of, i.e. discarded.

definitions.meaning: a fizzy soft drink, something sparkling
an informal name for one's father

explanation.surface: A child asking a father what is fizzing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop names both a fizzy soft drink and, colloquially, a father.

clue.text: Resort in desert for hotel guest

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A holiday resort in the desert suits someone staying at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' reads as a holiday spot but is re-sort: rearrange INDESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident in hotel language is a guest staying there, as against a visitor using the bar.

clue.text: Measurement across tier made in error

indicators.note: letters arranged in error are wrongly placed, so they are reordered here

explanation.surface: A cake tier was cut to the wrong width.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' rearranges TIERMADE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The diameter is the length of a straight line through the centre of a circle, from side to side.

indicators.note: something battered is knocked about, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A beaten-up sword kept indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is the name of the British royal family's dynasty, a royal house.

parts.note: something done and over is past

explanation.surface: A diner finished, asking whether that was a meal from Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: pasta is one of many Italian dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is the staple Italian food, so a typical dish in Milan.

clue.text: Tie game: would that be a letdown in medieval times?

definitions.text: would that be a letdown in medieval times?

parts.note: a tie is a match ending level, a draw

explanation.surface: A drawn match wondering if it would have disappointed people in the Middle Ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letdown' plays on a bridge literally let down across a castle moat, not a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's raising bridge was lowered over the moat to admit visitors, literally let down.

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means disgusting, highly offensive
rising in rebellion, as in an uprising

explanation.surface: A military attack by rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting means disgusting, and also taking part in a revolt, so a rebellious rising.

parts.note: the union is a wedding, and small scraps of torn paper are thrown over the newly married couple

explanation.surface: A trade union's document has been torn to pieces in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union tearing up an agreement; it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti is tiny bits of coloured paper thrown at weddings.

clue.text: Wine bottles in for orchestra member

indicators.note: to bottle something is to enclose it, so the wine holds the next piece inside

explanation.surface: Wine is bottled for a player in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a woodwind instrument found in every orchestra; here the instrument stands for its section.

clue.text: Crude trader I left in sultanate

indicators.note: one piece placed in the other means it goes inside

parts.note: Oman is an Arabian state ruled by a sultan

explanation.surface: A dealer in a Gulf sultanate departs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' looks like a description of the trader's manners; it is crude oil.
explanation.definitionFit: An oilman deals in or produces petroleum, the crude oil of the trade.

parts.note: a venue is the place where a meeting or event is held

explanation.surface: A street serving as a place to meet up.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a wide road or broad street, often lined with trees.

definitions.meaning: split as ..., it means relating to fish, which is what piscatorial means

explanation.surface: Asking whether an aloof person is an angler.
explanation.definitionFit: Offish is a variant of standoffish, cool and aloof; read in two words it is of fish.

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: to sink is to fall, drop down

explanation.surface: Something meant chiefly for a cracked sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges ITSFOR to give FIRSTO, and 'sink' is a verb here, not the kitchen basin.
explanation.definitionFit: First of all means before anything else, so primarily or chiefly.

clue.text: Long story a source of joy when upset

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned upside down, so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a gas is informal for something great fun

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale that turns into a source of gloom rather than joy.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse epic tale of heroes.

indicators.note: letters set wrong are out of place, so they are rearranged here

explanation.surface: Someone who felt something was wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Left is the opposite side to right, so it is the side that is not the right.

explanation.surface: A noisy spell spent in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinny sound is thin and metallic, the clattering quality of jangling.

clue.text: Some way out for the solver

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters, so the answer is concealed in them

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter offers the solver an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals the letters inside waY OUt.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue addresses its reader, so the person solving is you.

clue.text: Friend covers it up after I copy someone

indicators.note: one piece placed after another follows it in the answer
to cover something is to wrap round it, so the friend goes around the next piece

explanation.surface: A friend hides something after a person copies someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' only completes the phrase 'covers it up'; it does not turn anything round here.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or copy someone's manner.

clue.text: New Testament and Old Testament book written by first person, really

indicators.note: pieces written by the first person come after it, so it leads the answer

parts.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Bible books apparently penned by the speaker, said in earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: In truth is an adverb phrase meaning actually or in fact, just as really is.

parts.note: a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A good many people working hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Graft is informal British for toil, so to graft is to slog away.
